title: Copy/Paste/Replace
content: ### **List of Contents** #### **Copy and Paste** #### **Replace** #### Depending on the user's needs, copy and paste patterns or replace them only in the form of a specific pattern while maintaining the original properties. ### #### **Copy and Paste** 1. Click the ![Transform Pattern On.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/37879877879705)**Transform Pattern** or ![Edit Pattern On.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/37879877892633)E**dit Pattern tool** on the 2D toolbar. 2. Right-click on the pattern or Internal line to be copied. 3. Click the **Copy** (Ctrl+C) menu. 4. **Right-click on the 2D background and click the Paste **(Ctrl+V) menu. 5. Press the Shift key to place it on a vertical/horizontal/45˚ line or freely click anywhere you want. **📝****Note:** * Right-clicking during paste allows you to enter values for Interval/Number of Shapes/Position (Internal Line). * Patterns can be copied and pasted even between multi-run CLO programs. #### #### **Replace** 1. Right-click on the original pattern to be replaced. 2. Click the **Replace** menu. → The pattern is replaced with the copied pattern's segment point locations, curves, notches, baselines, pattern names, and grading information. → Sewing lines, Internal shapes, Graphics, Fabrics, Topstitching, Puckering, and buttons are maintained as the properties of the original pattern. **📝****Note:** Pattern replacement is only possible if the number of Segment points is the same. ![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/37879877900697) ### _**![Label.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/37879893509529)**_ _****_ Even if the old and new patterns have different segment points, you can easily replace them. 1. Right-click on the original pattern, internal line, internal shape, baseline, or baseline shape to be replaced. 2. Click **Replaced by** menu. → The original pattern or line is replaced with the new one's segment point locations, curves, notches, baselines, pattern names, and grading information. → Sewing lines, Internal shapes, Graphics, Fabrics, Topstitching, Puckering, and buttons are maintained as the properties of the original pattern. 3. Select the new pattern, internal line, internal shape, baseline, or baseline shape. → W**hen the number of segment points is the**same** , t**he replacement process will be completed automatically. 4. Click and match the Segment point from the original pattern to the new pattern. **→** W**hen the number of segment points**differs** , the Segment point matching action is required. → ****After matching enough Segment points,****t** he replacement process will be completed automatically. 5. **Press the**Enter** key to complete if enough core points have been matched or if there are no more points to match.** **📝 Note:** * If both the original and new patterns are half-symmetry, their center points will automatically align. * **For unclosed****internal shapes or baseline shapes, their endpoints are automatically matched. ** * **Press the Delete to cancel the last step, or****Press the Esc key to cancel all actions** Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide for users on how to efficiently copy, paste, and replace patterns in CLO 3D while preserving their original properties.

title: Freeze/Unfreeze
content: **Objective** Use this function to fasten patterns like solid objects. Deactivated patterns do not collide during simulation, however, frozen patterns do (they maintain collision). Therefore, it is better to use for draping multiple layered garments. For instance, draping and freezing inner garments first, then draping outerwear above helps avoid occasional instabilities. **Location** 3D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005490267/Toolbar_3D_Select_Move.png) **Select/Move** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005490287/Toolbar_2D_Pattern_Transform.png) **Transform Pattern** **Operation** 1. Select the tool/menu indicated above. 2. Right-click on the 3D or 2D pattern and click **Freeze/Unfreeze.** → The pattern selected is frozen/unfrozen. **※Note:** Right-click in the empty space of the 3D window and hover over **Show/Hide Color** , then click******Show Freeze** to show or hide the color applied during freeze. (ver 6.1)
content_description: This web page provides a guide on using the freeze/unfreeze function in 3D garment simulation to efficiently manage layered draping while maintaining collision for frozen patterns.

title: Convert to Curve Point
content: **Easily convert Segment Points on the patterns to Curve Points, or Curve Points to Segment Points** **** 1. Right-click on the segment point with ![Edit Pattern On.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/40166904035609) **Edit Pattern** tool or on the curve point with ![Edit Curve Point On.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/40166914856217)**Edit Curve Point** tool. 2. Click the **Convert to Curve Point**. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Maintain Curve** | Convert selected points by automatically adding curve points to maintain the curvature. If the segment is already smooth enough, no curved points will added. **Convert Only** | ![Label.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/40166904041881) Convert selected points without adding curve points. The segment result may be affected slightly. **📝****Note:** Clicking while holding down the Shift key on the keyboard allows for multiple selections.
content_description: Effortlessly switch between Segment Points and Curve Points in your designs with our intuitive conversion tool.

title: Open MetaHuman Body Types
content: ### **Objective** Select a desired MetaHuman body type and create an outfit for your MetaHuman in CLO before bringing the outfit to Unreal Engine as USD files. ### **Location** Library ▶ Click Avatar Folder ▶ MetaHuman ▶ Double click to download a desired MetaHuman body types ## **※ Note :** * Arms need to be bent on export in order for Unreal Engine's USD import pipeline to work properly. Once garments are ready to be exported, apply a pose named 'Default_Pose' in Pose folder to a desired MetaHuman body. * A pose named 'Apose' is provided in order for garments to be fit on a desired MetaHuman body with ease, especially around arms. * In Marvelous Designer versions below 2024.0.173, applying the two aforementioned poses to a MetaHuman body will result in the error message "No matching avatar" and will not be applied.
content_description: This web page guides users through selecting a MetaHuman body type, creating a custom outfit in CLO, and preparing it for export to Unreal Engine as USD files, while providing essential tips for pose application to ensure compatibility.

title: 3D State
content: **Record 3D state to compare or check your design process. ** 1. Open the History window on the left side of CLO. 2. Click the ![3D State.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/38099405049753) **Add 3D State** button to record 3D state as a project file. ![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/38099374825497) ### ![Label_Final.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/38099374826393) Preview the 3D state by hovering over the 3D state before opening it. ![3D State.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/38099939408409) ![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/38099374825497) 3. Double click the 3D state to open. 4. Right-click on the 3D state to rename, delete or add. **📝****Note:** When you save a project file(ZPRJ), the 3D State file is also saved with it. The more 3D files that are saved, the bigger the file is. It may slow down the speed when you open and save the file.
content_description: The purpose of this web page is to guide users on how to efficiently record and manage 3D states in CLO to enhance their design process.

title: Edit Sewing
content: **List of Contents** Edit Sewing Select Sewing Move Sewing Adjust Sewing Length Sewing Line Pop-Up Menu **Edit Sewing** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2bAz9JrDL_c \- Select and edit Sewing Lines in the 2D window. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022128067/mceclip0.png) **Edit Sewing** tool from the 2D toolbar. \- Or, navigate to the Main Menu and select Sewing ▶ **Edit Sewing.** ** Select Sewing** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SzXmYuh2bUs \- With the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022128067/mceclip0.png) **Edit Sewing** tool selected, click on the Sewing Line to be selected. \- The sewing Line will be bolded. \- When there are multiple Sewing Lines on the selected Pattern outline, pop-up menu showing all Sewing Line options will appear. \- Use the color chip in front of the Sewing Line name to choose the desired one. \- The Sewing Lines are ordered in an ascending order, arranging the latest to last. **Move Sewing** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5KY_402FwNA \- Select and drag the center of the Sewing Line. \- When the selected Sewing Line is on a symmetric Pattern, the second half of the Sewing Line on its symmetric pair will be moved simultaneously. **Adjust Sewing Length** * **Adjust Freely YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lHYoo3PXNCY **\- Select and drag one end point of the Sewing Line towards the desired direction. \- Only the selected half of the Sewing Line will be adjusted. To match the sewing length of the second half of the Sewing Line, repeat the same process as above. When adjusting the second half of the Sewing Line, a blue point will appear guiding the length of the first half of the Sewing Line. * **Adjust with Designated Value YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XBGxrO0iQdE ** \- Select and drag one end point of the Sewing Line towards the desired direction. \- While holding down the mouse, right-click to access the Moving Distance window. \- Enter the desired distance the point will be moved. **Sewing Line Pop-Up Menu** * **Access Right Click Pop-Up Menu YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=D47a6wpHlMY ** \- Right-click on the Sewing Line to be edited to access the pop-up menu. * **Select All with Same Property** \- Use this option to select all Sewing Lines with the same property. * **Fold Strength YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jb6FFxO9Es8 ** \- Select all Sewing Lines with the same Fold Strength value. * **Fold Angle YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QGA_K81Qgyw ** \- Select all Sewing Lines with the same Fold Angle value. * **Reverse Sewing YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=X-1VwGIDNvQ ** \- Reverse the direction notch of the selected Sewing Line. * **Delete Sewing YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5NJA7fVpyCA **\- Delete the selected Sewing Line. \- Right-click on the Sewing Line and select **Delete Sewing.** \- When deleting a Sewing Line, its pair will be deleted as well. \- Use this option when directional notches are twisted. * **Merge YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qE3cNLVGUjA ** \- Merge Patterns based on the selected Sewing Line. * **Add Point to Pattern on Start/ Add Point to Pattern on End YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q5ukIgMaCrA ** \- Add points to the Pattern outline based on the start or the end point of the Sewing Line. \- The point near the directional notch is the start point and the point far from the directional notch is the end point. * **Deactivate Sewing (Selected) YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dnJGBi2oI5c **\- Deactivate Sewing Lines to disable their functions. \- When the selected Sewing Line is deactivated, it will turn white. \- When the Simulation is activated, the Patterns with the deactivated Sewing Line will no longer sewn to each other. \- To activate the Sewing Line again, right click on the Sewing Line and select **Activate Sewing.** * **Hide Sewing YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9ksphJ8L94o ** \- Hide Sewing Lines in the 2D window. \- When the Sewing Lines are hidden, they will no longer appear in the 2D window. \- To show them again, right click on the Sewing Line and select **Show Sewing (All).** Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This webpage serves as a comprehensive guide for editing, selecting, moving, and adjusting sewing lines within a 2D design environment, complete with instructional videos for each function.

title: [View Control] Zoom In/Out, Rotation
content: **Objective** In CLO, the mouse wheel and the right button can be used to zoom in, zoom out, and rotate the screen. The Maya and 3Ds Max view control methods are also supported alongside the default view control method and interface can be modified as needed and use differently. ** Operation** **Move![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001788308/3D_Pan.png)** ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001762547/17______.png) Hold down the mouse wheel and drag to move the screen. If you are using Mac's Magic Mouse, please hold down the Alt key on the keyboard and click-and-drag the left mouse key. **Zoom In/Out![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001762587/3D_Zoom.png)** ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001762567/18______.png) Scroll down (zoom in) and up (zoom out) the mouse wheel to zoom in and zoom out the screen. Or, hold down Alt Key on the keyboard and the left button of the mouse simultaneously and drag up (zoom out) or down (zoom in). **※ Note:** Zoom in or zoom out using the + (zoom in) and - (zoom out) keys on the keyboard (ver2.4.0.) **Rotate![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001788288/3D_Rotate.png)** ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001788328/19___________.png) Hold down the right button of the mouse and drag to rotate the 3D window.
content_description: Explore the various 3D view controls in CLO, including zooming, moving, and rotating the screen using your mouse or keyboard shortcuts for enhanced navigation and customization.

title: How can I export FBX from CLO to APEXFiz?
content: **Question** I would like to know the recommended menu settings for FBX eport in CLO in order to use [Extract Patterns]. **Answer** [Extract Patterns] is a function that is only supported by the 3D OPTION of APEXFIz. Below is a menu of CLO software. ![FBX from CLO to APEXFiz.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/40661188216601) * Select necessary avatar and patterns. * Select multiple object, not single object. Export without combining vertex * Select [Thin] for thickness. * Select default [mm] for scale. * If textures are required, select embed media. * If textures are required, enter a file name and a folder name with half-width characters. * Create a unified UV map. At this time, all pattern UVs should be arranged within the 0-1 space in the UV editor, ensuring there is no overlap. Place the pattern UVs according to the knitting direction in APEXFiz, as this direction cannot be changed in the Extract Pattern menu. Textures with alpha(hair, eyelash, etc.) may not be imported correctly. Internal lines(design lines) cannot be imported. Stitch data will not be readable in APEXFiz.
content_description: This page provides essential menu settings for exporting FBX files from CLO to APEXFiz for effective use of the Extract Patterns function.

title: What is CLO Verified?
content: ### CLO OFFICIAL VERIFICATION CLO Verified is not a training, but an assessment of your skills in CLO Available for any CLO user with an Active Individual or Student License. No Enterprise Licenses can be used The test is broken into 3 different parts 1. Build a garment from a DXF pattern. 2. Correct a built garment that needs to be fixed/edited [similar to what you would be tasked with working in the industry]. 3. Combine the 2 garments to create a full look which you will render in CLO. A Visual Quality Standards document will be sent the week before the test that will provide you with guidelines for the project submission. You will receive all tech packs, patterns, and necessary materials the day of the test for all 3 parts. Once completed, you will be notified 2-3 weeks after the test by email. You will receive both the outcome (Pass/Fail) and feedback about the files you have submitted. ### CERTIFICATE & BADGE All participants who pass the test will receive the CLO Verified Certificate, the only CLO recognized certificate, as well as the CLO Verified Badge which can be added to LinkedIn or other social media to show others their proven level of CLO expertise. ### PRACTICE ASSESSMENT We recommend all users take the self-graded Practice Test before signing up and paying for the Official Verification. This test is very similar but slightly shorter than the Official Verification and includes a Visual Quality Standards Guide to help you. Passing the CLO Verified Practice Test does not guarantee that you will pass the Official Verification, but it does mean that you should possess the skills needed to do so. Also, passing the practice test does not make you CLO Verified. To become CLO Verified you must take and Pass the Official Verification which the CLO Academic Team reviews and grades. ### ****CURRENTLY THE CLO VERIFIED PRACTICE & OFFICIAL VERIFICATION ARE ONLY AVAILABLE IN ENGLISH**** ### THINK YOU’RE READY? * Do you use CLO regularly [15+ hours a week] with a focus on the CLO garment construction workflow? * Are you able to quickly troubleshoot issues within CLO? * Are you comfortable with Tech-Packs and Visual Quality Standards? To sign up for the Waitlist for alerts about upcoming tests and/or take the Practice Assessment please head over to the CLO Academy [HERE](https://www.cloacademy.online/catalog)
content_description: The CLO Official Verification page provides an assessment for CLO users to validate their skills through a structured test, culminating in a recognized certificate and badge for successful participants.

title: What languages does CLO come in?
content: **Question** What languages does CLO come in? **Answer** We currently offer CLO in English, Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Spanish, French, Italian, Portuguese, and much more. To change your language settings in CLO, go to Language in Settings, select the desired language, then restart the program to apply the changes. The manuals and video buttons connected within the CLO program may not be available in the set language. If you wish to change the language of the YouTube tutorial videos to your preferred language, you can first enable subtitles and then view them with automatic translation in your desired language. ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/40265359237017) Additionally, you can check tutorials on the dedicated CLO YouTube channels available in Portuguese, Spanish, and Japanese. * CLO Portuguese Youtube: [Here](https://www.youtube.com/@CLOBrasil) * CLO Spanish Youtube: [Here](https://www.youtube.com/@CLOesp) * CLO Japanese Youtube: [Here](https://www.youtube.com/@CLOJapan)
content_description: Discover the diverse language options available for CLO and learn how to customize your settings for an enhanced user experience.

title: Render Output Improvement (Graininess, Noise)
content: **Where to Start** Once your garment or look is finished, make sure you use the [Hi-Res Garment tool](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115012380608-Hi-Res-Garment) and simulate to see the realistic drape. Next, go to the **Render Menu ▶ Render** to enter the [Render Mode](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115014784747-Run-V-Ray-Render). Click to start an Interactive Render. As you view the preview, a good place to start is to use the default settings; ● set up the image size as desired ● use a **plain background** (with an image vignette if desired) ● **PNG file format** is lossless and will therefore give you better quality than the JPEG ● reset the lighting to Default (**Studio Low Contrast**) & activate **ground shadow** (this effect is a must when rendering a full avatar) ● **Windows** users: use the **GPU Engine** ● Noise Threshold set at **0.05** ● Max Render Time = **20 min** ● Light & Material Quality at **Medium** If you start here and create a final render, stop Interactive Render and click Final Render. Watch this complete and take note how long it takes. From here, you can make adjustments to the lighting and render properties to improve the image quality. **Further Considerations** Creating a beautiful image in CLO can be tricky at times. You need to balance the complexity of your project with the limitations of your hardware and the amount of time your computer will take to give you the final result. Here are a few things to consider; ● **How does your hardware match up to our[system requirements](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000307168-CLO-system-requirements-March-2024)?** It is better to go towards the _Recommended_ rather than _Minimum_. If your computer matches the minimum requirements, yes, it may work, but it will not be a good experience. You will quickly run into speed limitations not only while rendering, but with simulating as your garments get more complex. The amount of RAM in your computer will make the biggest difference with speed. ● **What materials did you use?** Are there any metals, sparkles, shiny areas on the fabrics, buttons, zippers, snaps, etc.? Anything that will reflect light while rendering can add more time to the rendering process. ● **Have you added accessories or objects in the scene that have glass or metal?** Did you create a “mirror” or place a ground plane that is very shiny? Think about your environment. It may be awesome to have a detailed room around your avatar and garment, but opting for a simple, plain background will not only reduce rendering time, but also focus the viewer’s attention on the garment. ● **How complex is the garment or garments making up the looks?** Is there visible internal layers or multiple layered garments? Are you using lots of buttons, zippers, graphics, prints, etc.? Is there puckering or have you activated Realistic Seamline while using the Fill tool? ● **What image size are you using?** It is recommended you pick from the pixel size options (640 x 480, etc.) as this will reduce the rendering time. The paper size layouts may seem attractive but the document/pixel ratios can cause a slowing of the rendering process. If needed, changing the resolution (ppi) will slow down the rendering process. ● **Check your[Render Properties](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115014899148-Edit-V-Ray-Render-Properties):** ○ Are you rendering **fur**? It is recommended to switch to CPU Engine to get better results, **but** it will take longer. So you need to decide whether the slower rendering is beneficial. ○ What is your **Noise Threshold**? Default 0.05, the lower you go, the better the details **but** it will take longer. ○ **Max Render Time** ; Based on all the variables, CLO will do the best it can with the time you have allotted. ○ **Light** and **Material Quality** will also affect the length of your render. **※****Note: **If you want to render an animation (rather than capturing the 3D window), always do a single render to start. The time it took to render that one image should be multiplied by the number of frames in the animation. ● Example: ○ image rendering time = 5 minutes ○ frames in animation = 450 ○ how long the render animation will take: 2250 minutes or 37.5 hours (a day and a half)
content_description: This webpage serves as a comprehensive guide to optimizing garment rendering in CLO, providing essential steps and considerations for achieving high-quality images efficiently.

title: Select Mesh (Box)
content: **List of Contents** Select Mesh (Box) Select Multiple Areas Delete Selection Invert Selection Select a Segment Select a Pattern **Select Mesh (Box) ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=44OLy1vRAzE \- Select and move 3D Garment Mesh as needed. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022721948/mceclip0.png) **Select Mesh****(Box)** tool from the 3D toolbar. \- Or, navigate to the Main Menu and select 3D Garment ▶ **Select Mesh (Box)** ** Select Multiple Areas ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qDiWjwmMSTg \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022721948/mceclip0.png) **Select Mesh (Box)** tool from the 3D toolbar. \- Patterns in the 2D window and 3D window will appear in yellow-green Mesh structure. \- Click and drag on the Pattern to create marquee box to select desired area. \- Hold down the Shift and Ctrl keys on the keyboard to select multiple areas on the 3D Garment. **Delete ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TQL0mobrWT8 \- To deselect particular areas, hold down the Ctrl key on the keyboard and click and drag to encompass the desired area in the 2D window. title: Zipper
content: **List of Contents** Zipper Creating Zipper Unzip/Zip Zipper Edit Zipper Tape/ Slider Property Zipper Tape/ Slider Right-Click Pop-Up Menu **Zipper** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1wDMdx1Fa-g \- Create and express zippers easily and quickly. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022759807/mceclip0.png) **Zipper** tool from the 3D toolbar. ** ****Creating Zipper** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Hc-HRRg4IGk \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022759807/mceclip0.png) **Zipper** tool from the 3D toolbar and navigate to the 3D window. \- The Pattern outlines and Internal Lines on the 3D Garment will appear as dashed lines. \- Hover the mouse over the Pattern outlines or Internal Lines where the Zipper will be placed. \- Click once and drag the mouse cursor along the Pattern outline or Internal Line. \- Double click to complete the first half of the Zipper. \- Hover the mouse over the Pattern outlines or Internal Lines where the other half of the Zipper will be placed. \- Repeat the same procedure. A blue dot will appear to guide the length of the first half of the Zipper. \- When the Zipper is established, the Zipper tape and the Zipper slider will appear along the designated Pattern outlines or Internal Lines. \- The Zipper slider will always be located at the starting position where Zipper was placed \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022760867/mceclip1.png) **Simulation** from the 3D Toolbar. \- The Zipper will fasten. **Unzip/ Zip Zipper** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yLlU1vC6pcE \- With Simulation off, select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022760907/mceclip2.png) **Select/Move** tool from the 3D toolbar to partially unzip or Zip the Zipper. \- Click on the Zipper slider, and it will be highlighted in yellow. \- Click and drag the Zipper slider along the Zipper tape. A grey slider will follow along the mouse to preview the location. \- Release the mouse to finalize Zipper slider’s location. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022760867/mceclip1.png) **Simulation** from the 3D toolbar. \- Only the designated part of the Zipper will fasten or unfasten. **Editing Zipper Tape/ Slider Property** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2DpM0NKENC8 \- Use the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022760907/mceclip2.png) **Select/Move** tool from the 3D toolbar to select either the Zipper tape or the Zipper slider. * **Zipper Tape YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eBunmqATU0E ** * **Width (MM) ** \- Type in a specific value to assign width to the Zipper tape. ** ** * **Thickness (MM) ** \- Type in a specific value to assign thickness to the Zipper tape. \- Change the Garment Rendering Style to ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022824148/mceclip4.png) **Thick Textured Surface** to see Zipper tape’s thickness. * **Fasten Zipper** \- Toggle on/off the option to completely Zip or unzip the Zipper. \- Toggle Off the **Fasten Zipper** option to unzip the zipper. * **Material - Texture** \- Change the texture of the Zipper tape. \- Add Normal Map and check on/off **Desaturation** to convert the texture into greyscale. * **Material - Color** \- Change the color of the Zipper tape. \- Adjust **Ambient Intensity** and **Diffuse Intensity** as needed. **Ambient Intensity** expresses the effect of ambient light. **Diffuse Intensity** controls the intensity of the applied texture image and color. \- Adjust **Specular Colo** r as needed. With the **Shininess** option, modify the sheen of the Zipper tape. \- Add Specular Map to assign how **Specular Color** is applied to the Zipper slider. \- Adjust **Emission Color** to set the color that emits from the Zipper tape. * **Fold** -**Strength:** set the strength of the fold of the Sewing Line between the Pattern and the Zipper. \- **Angle** : set the fold angle between the Zipper and the Pattern to express the fold . * **Particle Distance(mm)** \- Adjust Particle Distance for Zipper Tapes(ver4.1.0). * **Zipper Slider YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kuEU7A-rQzU ** * **Shape ** \- Choose the design of the Zipper slider. * **Size** \- Select the size of the Zipper slider from the provided presets, or type in a desired percentage to adjust manually. * **Fasten Zipper** \- Completely Zip or unzip the Zipper. \- Toggle On/Off the **Reverse Zipper Direction** option to locate the Zipper pull at either end of the Zipper. \- Toggle On/Off the **Move to Opposite Side** option to attach the Zipper pull to either half of the Zipper tape when the Zipper is unzipped. * **Material** \- Adjust provided options to add texture or colors to the Zipper slider. \- Adjust the **Opacity** to express the Zipper slider as translucent or solid. **Zipper Tape/ Slider Right-Click Pop-Up Menu** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TsS-HVmHOE0 \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022760907/mceclip2.png) **Select/Move** tool from the 2D toolbar and navigate to 2D window. \- Right click on the Zipper tape/ slider to be edited. \- The pop-up menu with options below will appear. * **Zipper Tape** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2HxuO5ZbOcI * **Delete** \- Delete the Zipper tape and slider. \- Select the Zipper seam line, right-click and select **Delete.** \- Or, Select the Zipper seam line, and hit the Delete Key on the Keyboard. * **Reverse (Right Clicked)** \- Similar to the Free Sewing tool, both halves of the Zipper tape need to be established in the same direction. If they are sewn incorrectly, the Zipper tape may twist. \- If Zipper appears to be deformed during Simulation, right-click and select **Reverse** to reverse the Sewing Line. * **Flip Normal (Right Clicked Teeth) ** \- Flip the fabric side of the Zipper tape in the 3D window. \- Select the Zipper Sewing Line, right-click and select **Flip Normal.** * **Deactivate/Freeze** \- Deactivate or Freeze the selected Zipper tape to fix and exclude the selected Zipper from Simulation. \- Right-click on Zipper seam line, select **Deactivate** or **Freeze.** \- To Reactivate or Unfreeze the deactivated/frozen Zipper tape, right-click the Zipper seam line again and select **Reactivate** or **Unfreeze.** * **Zipper Slider YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2az-u9u1ImQ** * **Delete -**Delete the Zipper Tape and Slider. \- Select the Zipper seam line, right-click and select **Delete.** \- Or, Select the Zipper seam line, and hit the Delete Key on the Keyboard. * **Deactivate/Freeze ****-** Deactivate or Freeze the selected Zipper Pull to fix and exclude the selected Zipper from Simulation. \- Right-click on Zipper Slider, select **Deactivate** or **Freeze.** Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page serves as a comprehensive guide for creating, editing, and managing zippers in 3D design, featuring step-by-step instructions and instructional videos.

title: Non-testable Fabrics for CLO Fabric Digitization Service
content: **Fabric Type** | **Physical Properties Testing** | **3D Image Scanning** | **Comments** ---|---|---|--- Short Fur | O | X | Short Fur can be expressed by setting the Fur option for the Material type of CLO Fabric. Long Fur | X | X | Long Fur can be expressed by setting the Fur option for the Material type of CLO Fabric. Feather Yarns | X | X | The decorations on the fabric make it difficult to measure stretch and bending accurately. Foil | O | X | Foil can be expressed by setting the Iridescene option for the material type of CLO Fabric. PVC | O | X | PVC can be expressed by setting the Iridescene option for the material type of CLO Fabric. Glitter | O | X | Glitter can expressed by setting the Glitter option for the material type of CLO fabric. Sequin | X | X | Sequin can be expressed using CLO. Pleats | X | X | Pleated fabric can be created by using CLO. Elastic Band | X | X | The unavailability of a suitable swatch size makes it difficult to measure physical properties. Wide Stripe Fabric (Made of different yarns) | X | X | The combination of the multiple properties makes it difficult to measure physical properties accurately in a single fabric. Dangling Embellishments | X | X | The decorations on the fabric make it difficult to measure stretch and bending accurately. Complicated Novelty Yarns | X | X | The decorations on the fabric make it difficult to measure stretch and bending accurately. Multi-layer Fabric | X | X | If the multiple fabric layers are only partially attached, it can affect the accuracy of physical property measurements. Crinkled Fabric | X | X | Fabric with processed crinkles is difficult to measure its stretch accurately. Openwork Lace | X | X | Fabric with a very loose weave is difficult to measure its stretch and bending properties.
content_description: This web page provides an overview of various fabric types and their associated physical properties testing capabilities, including limitations in measurement accuracy for specific materials.

title: Register API Plug-In
content: ### **Objective** By using [CLO API](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/360017616633), develop and add customized features to CLO. For example, develop a feature to collect necessary BOM information from a 3D garment produced in CLO. Then, add and use the customized feature in CLO. ** Location** Main Menu ▶ Settings ▶ User Settings ▶ **CLO API** ** Operation** 1. Follow the path indicated below: Main Menu ▶ Settings ▶ User Settings ▶ **CLO API** 2. Click the ![plus_button.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360019478214) **Add** button on the right top corner. → A File Explorer dialog appears where you can search *.dll or *.dylib files. 3. Select and **Open** the desired *.dll or *.dylib file. → The Register Plug-In window appears. 4. Refer to below and configure an UI for the plug-in to be added. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Name** | Name the plug-in. **Position** | Main Menu, child menus for the selected Main Menu, and any additional corresponding child menus appear in order. Select a desired menu and choose the plug-in's position in terms of the selected menu. 5. Click **OK** to complete the registration. ※Note: * Registered plug-ins also appear in below path: Main Menu ▶ Settings ▶ **Plug-in ** * Please [Contact Us,](https://www.clo3d.com/contact) if you have any questions.
content_description: This webpage serves as a comprehensive guide for developers to customize and integrate features into CLO using the CLO API, including detailed steps for registering plug-ins.

title: I forgot my license ID and password. (CLO below 2024.0)
content: * Please note that the below guideline applies to users who are using CLO version below 2024.0. If you are using CLO 2024.0 and above, please sign in with CLO-SET. **Question** I'm using CLO version below 2024.0 and I forgot my license ID and password. What should I do? **Answer** **Find license ID** To find your license ID, please follow the indicated guideline below: 1. Go to CLO website and click on '[Sign in](https://clo3d.com/en/signin)'. 2. If you forgot your ID but remember the email address used for sign-up, please use the email address to sign in. 3. You can find your ID on the [Account page](https://www.clo3d.com/accounts). However, if you forgot both the license ID and the email address used for signing in, please reach out to CLO via [Contact Us](https://www.clo3d.com/support/contactus) page. **Find Password** Please refer to the following article to reset your license password. * [How can I reset my password on CLO Web and the Software?](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/29936192175129-How-can-I-reset-my-password-on-CLO-Web-and-the-Software)
content_description: This web page provides guidance for users of CLO versions below 2024.0 on how to recover their license ID and reset their password.

title: Fold/Sew Pleats
content: **Objective** Create a variety of pleats, fold and sew them (ver2.3.0). ** Location** Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Pleats ▶ **Pleats Fold** / **Pleats Sewing** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001057348/________.png)**Pleats Fold** / ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001012867/________.png)**Pleats Sewing** ** Operation** **Pleats Fold** 1. Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. 2. Click to establish the initial point for the direction of the pleats, then double-click to establish the end point. → Pleats Fold window appears. 3. Select a desired type of pleats. → Depending on the selected pleats type, the Fold Angles of the Internal Lines are now being highlighted. **※****Note:** Yellow: Outside fold line (Fold angle of zero(0) degree), Light-blue: Inside fold line (Fold angle of 360 degree), Not highlighted: No fold line (Fold angle of 180 degree) 4. Check the **Reverse Direction** option as needed. **→** The direction of pleats being folded are now being reversed. 5. Click **OK** button to complete. **Pleats Sewing** 1. Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. 2. Click on the initial point and drag up to the end point of the seamline on the pleats Pattern. ※**Note:** In case of sewing the pleat pattern only, press enter to proceed to the next step. (ver 6.0) 3. On the pleats Pattern, click on the first Sewing Line to begin with, and move the mouse to the end point. → Sewing is now being established for every three(3) segments (the amount of segments needed to create each individual pleat). 4. Click on the end point to complete. → The color of the fluorescent sewing lines are now being changed for respective seam color, indicating that the sewing is being completed.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for creating and sewing various pleat styles in a 2D pattern design environment.

title: Can I change my subscription plan?
content: **Question** Can I change my subscription plan? **Answer** You can change the plan at least 24 hours before the next bill due to your current plan. To change the subscription plan from monthly to yearly (or vice versa), 1. Sign in to the CLO web and go to the [Subscription page](https://www.clo3d.com/en/accounts/subscription). 2. Click the "Change Plan" button. 3. Check the current subscription and plan type that will be changed. 4. Click the "Change" button. *Once you change your subscription plan, you can only change the plan again ONLY AFTER you complete purchasing the product on the starting date of the changed plans. Until then, you cannot cancel the changes. Only canceling a subscription is available. *If you change the plan, you will be charged the amount for the changed plan from the next payment date of the existing plan. *If you cancel the subscription, you cannot change the plan type. *Individual plans cannot be changed as student plans and vice versa. To change your license from CLO for Individuals to CLO for Business, please reach out to CLO via [Contact Us](https://www.clo3d.com/support/contactus).
content_description: This page provides essential information on how to change your subscription plan, including steps, restrictions, and billing details.

content: **Objective** Export Animation cache data. **※ Note:** You can export only the cache data of garments. ** Location** Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Export ▶ Animation * **Maya Cache (.mc) ** * **Maya Cache (.mcx) ** * **Point Cache 2 ** * **MDD Cache (Standard) ** * **MDD Cache (Maya/3ds Max)** ** Operation** 1. Click the tool/menu indicated. → The Save File window appears. 2. Select the desired file and click **OK**. → The Export window opens. 3. Set the full details and click **OK**. **** **Object** | **Unweld/Weld Object** Export the selected objects as unweld or weld objects. **※ Note: **This option is removed from 6.2 and above. ---|--- **Unweld** Exports the Vertex (points of the mesh) of the parts of the pattern that are sewn together into one line into multiple objects. ※ Thickness exports for quad meshes available beginning version. | **Weld** Combines the Vertex (points of the mesh) of the parts of the pattern that are sewn together into one line into one point. **Selected Pattern:** Weld based on the sewing line that connects the selected patterns. **Thin** Ensures that the thickness will not be exported even if the rendering thickness value is increased beforehand. | **Thick** Exports a pattern with its rendering thickness values in its increased state. **Combined UV Coordinates:** Exports all Garment Pattern texture data fit UV Coordinates ranging from 0 to 1. **※Note:** Unified Texture export multiple layers of texture information as a single UV texture information. **Scale** | Adjusts the scale of the file being exported when a value is entered or the desired unit from **Unit in file to import** is selected. **Axis Conversion** | Changes the directions of each axis of the object. **Animation** | Entire Area (saves all of the recorded garment animation.) | Play Area Only (saves only the play area garment animation.) **File** | **Save With Texture Files (.zip):** Exports the .obj file, .mtl file, and texture images used in the garment as one compressed file when exporting animation. **Save with Meta Data (.xml) :** Export the garment's pattern (Mesh), physical property, and sewing information as Meta Data (ver2.3.0). **Diffuse Color Combined on Texture:** Combine and save the garment's texture image and color as a single image (ver2.2.0). **Exclude Ambient Color (for Modo):** Exclude the Ambient color value when saving materials (ver2.2.0).
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide for exporting animation cache data for garments using various formats and options in the software.

the![Toolbar_Common_Sewing_Edit.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360010221313/Toolbar_Common_Sewing_Edit.png)**Edit Sewing** tool from the 3D toolbar. \- Right click on the Sewing the![Toolbar_Common_Sewing_Edit.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360010221313/Toolbar_Common_Sewing_Edit.png)**Edit Sewing** tool from the 3D toolbar. \- Right click on the Sewing Select the![Toolbar_Common_Sewing_Edit.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360010221313/Toolbar_Common_Sewing_Edit.png)**Edit Sewing** tool from the 3D toolbar. \- Right click on the menu. * Hide/Show Sewing \- Select the![Toolbar_Common_Sewing_Edit.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360010221313/Toolbar_Common_Sewing_Edit.png)**Edit Sewing** tool from the 3D toolbar. \- Right click on the Sewing Line to be hidden. \- Select Hide Sewing(Selected) from the pop-up menu. \- Select Sewing is hidden. \- To show the Sewing Line again, right click other Sewing Line. \- Select Show Sewing(All) from the pop-up menu. Go back to the List of Contents
